text: Some years later he secured. <break time="0.8s" /> An excellent post in Petersburg. <break time="0.8s" /> And, delighted with his rising fortunes. <break time="0.8s" /> He threw himself into decorating a new house. <break time="0.8s" /> Exactly as people of his rank. <break time="0.8s" /> Were expected to. <break time="0.8s" /> One day, climbing a stepladder. <break time="0.8s" /> To show an upholsterer. <break time="0.8s" /> How he wanted the curtains hung. <break time="0.8s" /> He slipped. <break time="0.8s" /> And struck his side. <break time="0.8s" /> Against the handle of the window frame. <break time="0.8s" /> Though the bruise seemed trivial at the time. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon afterward, however. <break time="0.8s" /> He began to notice. <break time="0.8s" /> A strange taste in his mouth. <break time="0.8s" /> And a dull pressure in his side. <break time="0.8s" /> Which neither rest nor medicine. <break time="0.8s" /> Nor the passing weeks could drive away. <break time="0.8s" /> The famous doctor he consulted. <break time="0.8s" /> Behaved exactly as Ivan Ilyich himself behaved in court. <break time="0.8s" /> Treating the case as a puzzle. <break time="0.8s" /> About a kidney or an appendix. <break time="0.8s" /> Rather than as a question. <break time="0.8s" /> Of whether his patient would live. <break time="0.8s" /> At home his complaints. <break time="0.8s" /> Only irritated his wife and daughter. <break time="0.8s" /> Who considered his illness an inconvenience. <break time="0.8s" /> Almost a fault. <break time="0.8s" /> As though he were suffering on purpose. <break time="0.8s" /> To spoil their busy social lives. <break time="0.8s" /> Long ago he had learned the logic lesson. <break time="0.8s" /> That Caius is a man. <break time="0.8s" /> That all men are mortal. <break time="0.8s" /> And that Caius is therefore mortal. <break time="0.8s" /> And it had always seemed perfectly correct. <break time="0.8s" /> As applied to Caius. <break time="0.8s" /> He, however, had never been Caius. <break time="0.8s" /> Or any abstract man. <break time="0.8s" /> But little Vanya. <break time="0.8s" /> With a mother and a father. <break time="0.8s" /> With toys and a striped leather ball. <break time="0.8s" /> And for such a being to die. <break time="0.8s" /> Seemed impossible. <break time="0.8s" /> He tried to push the thought away. <break time="0.8s" /> By returning to his work. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet in the middle of a trial. <break time="0.8s" /> It would quietly appear again. <break time="0.8s" /> Standing before him. <break time="0.8s" /> And looking straight into his eyes.
